steps: The doctor met two men while treating their sick mother and then visited their home regularly for about a month.
They said they knew a baba (tantrik) and persuaded him to meet the baba.
At the meeting they rubbed a lamp and presented a man in costume as a djinn; the article says he had no real power.
The doctor paid Rs 31 lakh as a down payment; the men said the lamp would sell for Rs 1.5 crore and bring wealth, fame and better health.
The doctor complained on 25 October (2020 inferred from publication); police arrested the two men and recovered a golden lamp.
cases.amount_lost: Rs 31 lakh (down payment)
cases.outcome: Two men arrested; golden lamp recovered; police said they had cheated several others and were searching for a linked woman
cases.reporting_route: complaint by the doctor to Meerut police (station not named)

cases.title: Fake 'hidden crores' tantrik money-moving gang caught in sting, Indore
cases.location: Indore, Madhya Pradesh, India (meeting at a shop in Pigdamber; arrest at the leader's flat)
steps: The gang targeted superstitious people who believed in black magic and tantriks.
The leader showed a video of currency bundles claimed to be hidden crores in a godown; only the top note in each bundle was real.
The gang said a tantrik could physically move the money, which they would hand over as payment for their fee.
Small magic tricks built the victim's confidence; after the fee was collected the gang disappeared.
A Bhopal-based reporter complained to the Crime Branch; a friend posed as a tantrik and the Crime Branch arrested three men at the leader's flat.
cases.amount_lost: Not reported for past victims; the sting was quoted a Rs 50,000 fee; victims reportedly charged Rs 50,000 to Rs 1 lakh each
cases.outcome: Three men arrested; counterfeit Rs 2,000 notes (15 bundles) and Rs 500 notes (230 bundles) and the car seized; questioning to identify other victims
cases.reporting_route: a news reporter's complaint to the Crime Branch led to a police trap

cases.title: Self-styled baba's Rs 100 crore 'money doubling' dera scam, arrested in Faridabad
cases.location: Haryana, India (accused from Kurukshetra; arrested in Faridabad)
steps: He set up a religious dera in Haryana and cheated people through claimed black magic.
He promised devotees their money would be doubled quickly.
He handed out candies presented as sacred offerings (parsad).
He allegedly took about Rs 100 crore from people; 31 FIRs were registered against him.
He stayed on the run for about a year before Haryana Police arrested him in Faridabad.
cases.amount_lost: About Rs 100 crore (alleged)
cases.outcome: Arrested; 10-day police remand ordered by a local court; no further outcome reported
cases.reporting_route: not reported

cases.title: Madhya Pradesh tantrik takes gold necklace from couple on pretext of puja
cases.location: Ujjain, Madhya Pradesh, India (victims from Indore)
steps: A tantrik invited a woman and a man from Indore to Ujjain, saying a puja was needed.
In the name of the puja he took a 7-tola gold necklace worth about Rs 2.5 lakh from them.
After the cheating, two companions of the tantrik allegedly assaulted the victims.
One victim complained at Nanakheda police station; the tantrik and the two companions were arrested.
cases.amount_lost: Gold necklace (7 tola), valued at about Rs 2.5 lakh
cases.outcome: Three accused arrested; gold necklace and the Bolero used in the incident recovered
cases.reporting_route: police station (Nanakheda, Ujjain)

cases.title: Kerala man posing as temple priest takes gold and cash from family for 'rituals'
cases.location: Palakkad district, Kerala, India (family met at a temple in Palani, Tamil Nadu)
steps: He posed as an ascetic temple priest, claimed to perform pujas at Guruvayur temple, and approached devotees at temples.
He offered rituals to fix a family's troubles, telling them that burying the lady of the house's jewellery in a cloth sack in their courtyard would bring jobs and end problems.
He took Rs 10,000 for the puja and left with 2.5 sovereigns of gold, which he did not return.
After the family complained, police phoned him posing as clients needing a ritual in Palakkad, and arrested him when he came.
cases.amount_lost: Rs 10,000 cash plus 2.5 sovereigns of gold
cases.outcome: Arrested after a police phone sting; police said he faces similar cases in Ernakulam and Thrissur and that many victims did not complain for fear of ridicule
cases.reporting_route: family complaint to police; arrest at Kuzhalmannam police station, Palakkad

cases.title: South Florida psychic sentenced for $1.6 million curse-lifting fraud on a Houston woman
cases.location: South Florida, USA (victim in Houston, Texas)
steps: She met the victim in Houston in 2007 while presenting herself as a psychic and fortune teller.
She told the victim a curse had been placed on her and her family.
She said buying items such as crystals and candles was needed to lift the curse.
She warned that refusing would bring harm to the victim and her family.
The scheme ended in 2014, when she admitted there was no curse.
cases.amount_lost: About $1.6 million from one victim
cases.outcome: Guilty plea; sentenced to 40 months in federal prison; ordered to pay $1.6 million restitution
cases.legal_sections: One count of wire fraud (guilty plea)
cases.reporting_route: not reported (federal prosecution)

cases.title: Psychic accused of evil-spirit scam against 67-year-old man who sold his house and car, York Region, Ontario
cases.location: York Region, Ontario, Canada (accused from Toronto)
steps: A woman presenting herself as a psychic, whom the victim had known for about four years, told him evil spirits were in his home.
She said he had to sell the house and transfer the money to her account, to be held until the spirits were removed.
He sold the house and transferred the money; he also sold his car and used credit and other sources to pay later demands.
She asked for another $6,000, saying she would burn it to ward off the spirits.
Police say the earlier funds were not returned; the investigation began in November 2017 and charges were announced in October 2018.
cases.outcome: 27-year-old woman charged; no outcome reported
cases.legal_sections: Pretending to practise witchcraft; fraud over $5,000; possession of property obtained by crime
cases.reporting_route: police investigation (York Regional Police)

cases.title: Astrologer allegedly cheated client of Rs 1.5 lakh for puja to improve her mother's health, later stabbed her; bail refused
cases.location: Delhi, India
steps: A woman, the astrologer's client, alleged he harassed her for about one and a half years and cheated her of Rs 1.5 lakh, supposedly to improve her mother's health and solve her personal problems.
On 4 May 2018 he allegedly took her to a hotel in Delhi, saying a puja of about three and a half hours would be performed.
He allegedly chanted mantras for about two hours, then asked her to sit on the bed and touched her inappropriately.
He allegedly struck her neck with a knife and stabbed her again when she tried to run; she suffered seven injuries, three on the neck.
The prosecution argued he may have been attempting a human sacrifice; the Delhi High Court dismissed his bail plea on 12 August 2021.
cases.amount_lost: Rs 1.5 lakh (as alleged by the complainant)
cases.outcome: Bail dismissed by the Delhi High Court on 12 August 2021 because the complainant's cross-examination was pending; accused given liberty to apply again afterwards
cases.reporting_route: not reported

cases.title: Haryana-origin baba extorts woman over a son-conception remedy, Hyderabad
cases.location: Tolichowki and Humayunnagar, Hyderabad, Telangana, India
steps: A woman with three daughters was pressured by her husband for a son and approached a self-described black-magic practitioner.
He said an evil spirit was in her and demanded Rs 1 lakh to remove it.
He demanded another Rs 1 lakh to help her conceive a boy, and she paid without telling her family.
After three months, with no conception, he demanded more money and asked her for sex.
When she refused, he threatened to kill her daughters using his powers; she approached the DCP West Zone, who laid a trap and police arrested him.
cases.amount_lost: Rs 2 lakh, plus a further unspecified amount demanded
cases.outcome: Arrested by Humayunnagar police; sent to judicial remand
cases.reporting_route: complaint to DCP West Zone, who laid a trap; police booked a case

cases.title: Self-styled astrologer arrested for cheating people over personal and marital problems, LB Nagar
cases.location: LB Nagar, Hyderabad, Telangana, India
steps: A man who had hosted programmes on private TV channels posed as an astrologer.
Police said he claimed to solve marital problems and trapped women this way (no further detail given).
People paid him money to resolve personal problems; LB Nagar police arrested him for allegedly cheating them.
Police seized a fake pistol, 2 tolas of gold, 5 kg of silver, Rs 5 lakh cash, an Innova car and a fake CBI identity card.
cases.amount_lost: Not reported (cash and valuables were seized from the accused; victims' losses not stated)
cases.outcome: Arrested; no further proceedings described
cases.reporting_route: not reported

cases.title: Man posing first as NGO worker, then as face-reading astrologer, takes Rs 20 lakh and gold from mother of epileptic child on a curse pretext, Bengaluru
cases.location: Bengaluru, Karnataka, India (Vijayanagar police)
steps: In November 2016 the accused approached a 35-year-old woman as an NGO worker collecting donations for differently-abled children; she donated Rs 200 and her phone number was on the receipt.
He later presented himself as an astrologer who could read faces; her son had epilepsy and had not improved with several doctors.
He told her a curse (dosha) and a spell were on her and said he could remove it if she had sex with him; a woman was allegedly made to call her to reinforce the claim.
He allegedly drugged her with narcotic-laced cigarettes, recorded her while unconscious and used the video to say her body was cursed; police allege seven assaults.
He took about Rs 20 lakh in cash and gold jewellery, saying it was for rituals to help her son.
She realised the fraud when he switched off his phone, told her husband and filed a complaint; police arrested him and recovered Rs 14 lakh and 300 g of gold jewellery.
quoted_lines: claimed himself to be an astrologer and sexually exploited her seven times
cases.amount_lost: About Rs 20 lakh in cash and gold jewellery (gold quantity lost not reported)
cases.outcome: Arrest; police recovered Rs 14 lakh cash and 300 g gold jewellery; charges and court proceedings not reported
cases.reporting_route: Complaint to police (Vijayanagar) after she told her husband; no helpline or portal named

cases.title: Fake swami drugs devotees on temple pilgrimages to take cash and gold under a money-doubling promise, Hyderabad
cases.location: Hyderabad, Telangana, India (West Zone police; a family was drugged at a lodge in Panjagutta; accused from East Godavari district, Andhra Pradesh)
steps: Posing as a swami, the accused performed poojas and, police said, convinced devotees of 'superhuman powers' to double cash and gold.
He told victims they had a bad omen in their families and asked them to bring valuables to rituals.
He invited victims on pilgrimages to temples and gave them drinks laced with sleeping pills during rituals.
When they became dizzy he took their gold and cash; in the Panjagutta case a family was drugged at a lodge and gold and cash taken from them.
West Zone police arrested him and recovered 1.5 kg of gold and Rs 40 lakh; he is linked to 11 fraud cases across Telangana and Andhra Pradesh.
quoted_lines: He convinces devotees about his superhuman powers to double cash and gold.
Then he makes them take drinks laced with sleeping pills.
cases.amount_lost: Not reported per victim (police said several people were cheated of large sums)
cases.outcome: Arrest; 1.5 kg gold and Rs 40 lakh recovered; linked to 11 fraud cases; he started the business in 2011, was arrested in 2013 and released, then resumed; sent to judicial custody
cases.reporting_route: not reported

cases.title: Self-described healer advertising magical cures on TV; Madras High Court refuses to quash fraud and cheating cases
cases.location: Tamil Nadu, India (Madras High Court)
steps: The accused allegedly claimed supernatural powers to cure all ailments and advertised on several TV channels.
He allegedly claimed to have been blessed with magical powers by a goddess.
His daughter and son-in-law allegedly also took money from victims while giving treatment.
After his arrest was reported in the media, more complaints came in and the Commissioner of Police moved several cases from local stations to the Central Crime Branch.
The Madras High Court held that return of money does not erase the offence, dismissed the petition to quash the FIRs (stayed since 2010 and 2011) and directed expeditious investigation.
quoted_lines: return of money cannot efface the offence of fraud and cheating committed by quacks
cases.amount_lost: not reported (described only as large sums)
cases.outcome: Petition to quash dismissed by a single-judge bench; investigation to proceed expeditiously; several cases transferred to the Central Crime Branch
cases.legal_sections: not reported (article describes the offences as fraud and cheating; court relied on State of Haryana v. Bhajan Lal)
cases.reporting_route: not reported (complaints followed media reports of the arrest)

cases.title: Fake tantrik fakes money-doubling demos, Rs 1.33 crore lost to a businessman, Hyderabad
cases.location: Hyderabad, Telangana, India (Banjara Hills police); first meeting at a club in Bengaluru
steps: A friend introduced a businessman to a self-styled tantrik at a club in Bengaluru, where he was said to have 'magically' doubled Rs 2 lakh.
A demo puja was held at the businessman's house; police say small sums were shown appearing from nowhere, funded by Rs 1.7 lakh borrowed from friends and Rs 70,000 from the introducing friend.
The tantrik persuaded the businessman to hand over larger sums for doubling; the businessman lost Rs 1.33 crore.
Victims were drugged with a mixture of datura and white sesame seeds and the tantrik fled with the money.
Police arrested the tantrik and two helpers and seized Rs 1,19,50,000, to be deposited in court; income-tax officials sought the cash; the introducing friend is absconding.
quoted_lines: after drugging them with a mixture of datura and white sesame seeds
cases.amount_lost: Rs 1.33 crore
cases.outcome: Arrest of the tantrik and two helpers; Rs 1,19,50,000 seized; income-tax department sought possession claiming tax owed; introducing friend absconding
cases.reporting_route: not reported
